pages.text: Donroe Doctrine

Donroe Doctrine


• President Donald Trump has formally revived and expanded
the Monroe Doctrine, a policy dating back to the 19th century.

• The doctrine, originally aimed at blocking European
colonization in the Western Hemisphere, is being reinterpreted
for modern geopolitics.

• Its revival signals a more assertive U.S. approach to influence
and security in the Americas.

Donroe Doctrine

What was the Monroe Doctrine?

• The Monroe Doctrine was issued on December 2, 1823, by U.S.
President James Monroe, declaring the Western Hemisphere an
exclusive sphere of influence of the United States.

• It warned European powers against any further colonization or
political intervention in the Americas, stating such actions would
be viewed as hostile to U.S. interests.

• The doctrine was largely drafted by Secretary of State John
Quincy Adams and rested on four core principles.

•.
                                   Donroe Doctrine


     • Non-Colonization: The American continents were closed to any
     new European colonies.

     • Two Spheres Theory: A clear distinction was drawn between the
     “Old World” (Europe) and the “New World” (the Americas),
     asserting they should not interfere in each other’s political systems.

     • Hands-Off Warning: Any attempt by European monarchies to
     extend their political influence in the Western Hemisphere would be
     considered “dangerous to our peace and safety”.

Donroe Doctrine


• U.S. Neutrality: In return, the United States pledged not to
interfere in European wars or internal European affairs.

• A major motivation was to prevent Spain, backed by the Holy
Alliance (Russia, Prussia, Austria), from reclaiming newly
independent Latin American states.

• The doctrine also aimed to curb Russian expansion, particularly
Russia’s claims along the Pacific Northwest coast under the Ukase
of 1821.

Donroe Doctrine


• By issuing a unilateral declaration rather than a joint statement
with Britain, the U.S. sought to assert its own sovereignty and future
expansionist ambitions.

• Initially, the doctrine lacked enforcement power, as the U.S.
military was weak; in practice, it was upheld by the British Royal
Navy, which shared an interest in limiting rival European powers.

• The doctrine was significantly expanded by President Theodore
Roosevelt through the Roosevelt Corollary (1904).

Donroe Doctrine


• The Roosevelt Corollary asserted the U.S. right to exercise
“international police power” in Latin America, transforming the
doctrine from defensive to interventionist.

• The doctrine became a foundation of U.S. foreign policy toward
Central and South America, framing the region as America’s
strategic “backyard”.

• U.S. Marines were deployed to Santo Domingo (1904),
Nicaragua (1911), and Haiti (1915), officially to prevent European
involvement, as noted by the National Archives.

Donroe Doctrine

Journey of Monroe Doctrine –

• The Monroe Doctrine represents a 203-year evolution from a
defensive warning in the 19th century to a justification for U.S.
hemispheric dominance in the 21st century.

• It was originally designed to prevent European colonization in the
Americas but was repeatedly reinterpreted to legitimize U.S.
intervention in Latin American affairs.

• In 1823, the doctrine was articulated by President James Monroe
and largely drafted by Secretary of State John Quincy Adams.

Donroe Doctrine


• It established two distinct spheres of influence: the “New World”
(the Americas) and the “Old World” (Europe).

• The core principles included a U.S. pledge of neutrality in
European wars and a warning that any European attempt to colonize
or oppress independent American states would be treated as a
hostile act against the United States.

• Initially, the doctrine was largely symbolic and aspirational, as
the U.S. lacked sufficient military power, and European powers mostly
ignored it until the mid-19th century.

Donroe Doctrine


• During the 1840s, under President James K. Polk, the doctrine
was invoked alongside Manifest Destiny to justify westward
expansion and the Mexican–American War.

• In 1904, President Theodore Roosevelt expanded the doctrine
through the Roosevelt Corollary, converting it from a defensive
policy into an assertion of “international police power.”

• The Roosevelt Corollary justified U.S. intervention in Latin American
countries facing chronic instability, debt crises, or alleged
wrongdoing, leading to occupations in Cuba, Nicaragua, and
Haiti.

Donroe Doctrine


• During the Cold War, the doctrine was reframed as a tool to
counter communism in the Western Hemisphere.

• In 1962, President John F. Kennedy relied on Monroe Doctrine
logic to demand the removal of Soviet missiles from Cuba during
the Cuban Missile Crisis.

• In the 1980s, President Ronald Reagan invoked the doctrine to
oppose and intervene against leftist governments and
movements in Central America.

Donroe Doctrine

Why in news?

• Following the early-morning capture of Venezuelan President
Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores, President Donald Trump held
a press conference justifying the operation through long-standing U.S.
foreign policy principles.

• Trump stated that the operation was consistent with the Monroe
Doctrine, which he described as guiding U.S. policy for over 200
years.

Donroe Doctrine


• Speaking on January 3, Trump argued that Venezuela had violated
core U.S. security principles by hosting foreign adversaries,
acquiring offensive weapons, and seizing and selling American
oil assets.

• He claimed these actions constituted a direct breach of U.S.
hemispheric norms dating back to the 19th century.

• Trump said the U.S. response not only followed the Monroe Doctrine
but went beyond it, declaring that the policy had been
“superseded.”

Donroe Doctrine


• He publicly introduced the term “Donroe Doctrine”, asserting it as
an expanded and modernized version of the original doctrine.

• Trump stated that the Monroe Doctrine was “a big deal,” but
emphasized that his administration had taken it “a real lot further.”

• The remarks marked a clear reversal from 2013, when then-
Secretary of State John Kerry, under President Barack Obama,
declared that the “era of the Monroe Doctrine is over.”

Donroe Doctrine

What is the Donroe Doctrine?

• As of January 2026, the “Donroe Doctrine”—a portmanteau of
Donald Trump and the Monroe Doctrine—has emerged as the
cornerstone of the Trump administration’s foreign policy,
presenting a militarized reinterpretation of the 1823 Monroe
Doctrine.

• The doctrine asserts that the Western Hemisphere is an
exclusive American sphere of influence, rejecting the presence or
strategic expansion of external powers.

Donroe Doctrine


• Following the January 3, 2026 capture of Nicolás Maduro, the
administration released a formal framework outlining the doctrine’s
operational provisions.

• The doctrine introduces an “Anti-Adversary” clause, explicitly
barring China, Russia, and Iran from establishing military bases,
controlling critical infrastructure such as ports or mines, or entering
security pacts anywhere in the Americas.

• It claims the U.S. right to “nationalize or transition” strategic
assets in the hemisphere owned by rival powers if deemed a threat
to U.S. national security.

Donroe Doctrine


• This asset-reclamation principle was cited as the main justification
for the seizure of Venezuelan oil fields during Operation
Absolute Resolve.

• The doctrine unveils a “Trump Corollary”, expanding beyond the
1904 Roosevelt Corollary by asserting a right to preemptive
intervention to prevent “adversarial drift” toward rival global powers.

• It redefines “The Americas” to include Greenland, arguing that its
position on the North American tectonic plate places it under the
doctrine’s protective and possessory scope.

Donroe Doctrine


• A central strategic objective is total energy dominance, seeking
control over the hemisphere’s oil, gas, and mineral reserves by
sidelining foreign influence in Venezuela and securing Arctic routes
through Greenland.

• The doctrine categorizes drug trafficking as a form of “hostile
invasion”, labeling certain countries as “narco-states.”

Donroe Doctrine


• It authorizes unilateral U.S. military and law-enforcement
operations across borders without host-nation consent if a state is
deemed unable or unwilling to control narco-trafficking.

• Another core goal is to monopolize trade and investment,
pressuring Latin American nations to disengage from China’s Belt
and Road Initiative and align exclusively with U.S. capital,
security, and infrastructure systems.
Trump claims Greenland

Trump claims Greenland


• Recently, In January 2026, President Donald Trump
escalated his long-standing push to acquire Greenland, calling it
an “absolute necessity” for the United States.

• He framed Greenland’s acquisition as a “national security
priority”, citing strategic concerns in the Arctic region.

• The rhetoric marked a sharp intensification compared to earlier
proposals, moving from diplomatic interest to urgent strategic
necessity.

Trump claims Greenland

Greenland –

• Greenland is the world’s largest island, located in the
North Atlantic Ocean.

• It is officially called Kalaallit Nunaat, meaning “Country of the
Greenlanders.”

• The island is part of the Kingdom of Denmark but has a
home-rule government responsible for most domestic affairs.

Trump claims Greenland


• The Greenlandic people are primarily Inuit, identifying
themselves as:
➢ Kalaallit (West Greenlanders),
➢ Inugguit (from the Thule district),
➢ Iit (East Greenlanders).

• Nearly 90% of Greenlanders are Inuit, with some European
ancestry. Over 10% of the population are Danish, mostly
born in Denmark.

• The capital city is Nuuk (Godthåb).

Trump claims Greenland



• The official languages are:
➢ Kalaallisut (West Greenlandic), the most widely spoken Inuit
   dialect,
➢ Danish,
➢ English is also commonly spoken.

• Greenlandic dialects include:
➢ Tunumiit (East Greenlandic),
➢ Inuktun or Avanersuarmiutut (Polar/Northern
   Greenlandic).

Trump claims Greenland



• The official religion is Evangelical Lutheranism, followed by
about two-thirds of the population.

• About one-third of the population follows other forms of
Christianity. Traditional beliefs, including shamanism, are still
practiced by a small minority.

• Greenland is known for its vast tundra and immense
glaciers.

Trump claims Greenland

History of Greenland –

• The Inuit are believed to have migrated to northwest
Greenland from North America, using the Canadian Arctic
islands as stepping-stones, with cultures such as
Independence I, Saqqaq, and Thule known from various
migration waves.

• In 982, Erik the Red, a Norwegian banished from Iceland,
settled in Greenland and later named it Greenland in an attempt
to attract settlers. His son Leif Eriksson brought Christianity to
Greenland in the 11th century.

Trump claims Greenland


• The Norse settlements in Greenland, including the East
and West Settlements, thrived in the 11th and 12th
centuries, reaching populations of 3,000-6,000 but began to
decline by the 14th century, possibly due to a cooling
climate.

• From the 16th to 17th centuries, Dutch and English
whalers interacted with Greenland’s population, but formal
colonization did not occur until 1721, when Hans Egede
founded a trading company and Lutheran mission in Nuuk.

Trump claims Greenland



• Denmark assumed a monopoly on trade in 1776, closing
Greenland’s coast to foreign access until 1950, while also trying
to modernize Greenland’s systems without exploiting its people.

• Greenland was under U.S. protection during World War II
and was returned to Denmark in 1945, with subsequent reforms
beginning in the 1950s to improve the economy, transportation,
and education.

Trump claims Greenland


• By the 21st century, growing support for greater
autonomy emerged, partly due to concerns about U.S. military
activities in Greenland, such as the Thule Air Base missile
defense system and the nuclear accidents during the Cold War.

• A 2008 referendum saw over 75% of Greenlanders
support greater autonomy, leading to expanded control over
foreign affairs, immigration, justice, and natural
resources, with the potential to reduce Greenland's economic
dependence on Denmark.

Trump claims Greenland


• In 2014, Hammond resigned after misusing government
funds and was replaced by Kim Kielsen, whose party, Siumut,
formed a new coalition despite opposition parties gaining seats.

• In 2016, Kielsen’s coalition splintered, leading to a new
government formed with the IA and Partii Naleraq, which
continued to navigate political challenges, including airport
funding disputes.

Trump claims Greenland


Why in news –

• President Donald Trump and his advisers are considering a
“range of options” to acquire Greenland, including the
possible use of the U.S. Military, according to White House
Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, speaking on January 6,
2026.

• In January 2026, Trump described the acquisition of
Greenland as an “absolute necessity” and a national
security priority for the United States.

Trump claims Greenland

• Following the January 3, 2026 U.S. military operation in
Venezuela that led to the capture of Nicolás Maduro,
administration officials suggested similar “decisive action”
could be applied in pursuit of Greenland.

• A senior U.S. official, speaking anonymously, confirmed that
internal discussions include multiple acquisition paths rather than
a single strategy.

• Options under consideration include an outright U.S. purchase
of Greenland, a Compact of Free Association (COFA)
similar to agreements with Palau, or potential annexation.

Trump claims Greenland


• A COFA arrangement would stop short of making Greenland
part of the United States, preserving limited autonomy while
placing defense and foreign policy under U.S. control.

• No potential purchase price for Greenland has been disclosed
by the administration.

• Trump revived the idea publicly in December 2024, declaring
on social media that U.S. ownership and control of
Greenland is essential for “National Security and Freedom
throughout the World.”

Trump claims Greenland


• Speaking aboard Air Force One, Trump said the U.S. needs
Greenland for “economic security”, reinforcing both strategic
and financial justifications.

• Vice President JD Vance, during a visit to Greenland in
March 2025, stated it was official U.S. policy to seek changes
in the island’s relationship with Denmark, while acknowledging
that Greenlanders should decide their own future.

• Public opinion in Greenland remains firmly opposed, with
85% of Greenlanders rejecting becoming part of the United
States, according to Reuters.

Trump claims Greenland

Reasons behind such claim –

• Greenland is the world’s largest island, home to more than
56,000 people, and is an autonomous territory of
Denmark.

• The capital, Nuuk, is geographically closer to New York than
to Copenhagen, Denmark's capital.

• Greenland holds a key geopolitical position, sitting between
the US and Europe and forming part of the Greenland-
Iceland-United Kingdom gap, a strategic maritime region.

Trump claims Greenland


• The Northwest Passage shipping lane runs along its coast,
offering potential economic and strategic advantages as ice
melts.

• The island is critical for US security, particularly to counter
potential attacks from Russia, as noted by experts.

• The US has a 1951 defense treaty with Denmark, allowing
the establishment of the Pituffik Space Base in northwest
Greenland, equipped with a missile warning system and
positioned midway between Moscow and New York.

Trump claims Greenland


• Historically, the US expressed interest in purchasing Greenland:
In 1867, during President Andrew Johnson’s tenure, Greenland
was considered for purchase alongside Alaska.

• In 1946, the Truman administration offered $100 million for
the island.

• Greenland is rich in natural resources, including oil, gas, and
rare earth metals, which are essential for electric vehicles,
wind turbines, and military equipment.

Trump claims Greenland


• China dominates global rare earth production, prompting US
interest in Greenland to reduce reliance on China.

• Melting ice due to climate change has opened up shipping
routes and increased the potential accessibility of Greenland’s
resources, though these routes remain treacherous.

• Arctic shipping rose 37% between 2014 and 2024,
according to the Arctic Council, driven in part by the melting ice.

Trump claims Greenland


• The loss of Greenland’s ice contributes to global sea level rise
but also presents perceived economic opportunities for
resource extraction.

• Experts note that climate change has not significantly improved
resource accessibility but has instead made these resources
more necessary for global industries.

Trump claims Greenland


• Also, Trump has justified the push on security grounds,
claiming the U.S. needs Greenland to counter Russian and
Chinese influence in the Arctic, alleging the island is
surrounded by Russian and Chinese ships.

• He further argued that Denmark lacks the capability to
adequately defend Greenland, making U.S. involvement
necessary.

Trump claims Greenland

The response –

• Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen warned that any
U.S. attack on Greenland, a NATO ally, would effectively end
the transatlantic alliance.

• Greenland’s Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen
rejected U.S. claims outright, calling them “fantasies of
annexation”.

• Nielsen stressed that Greenland’s status must be governed by
international law and mutual respect for sovereignty.

Trump claims Greenland



• On January 6, 2026, leaders of France, Germany, Italy,
Poland, Spain, and the UK, along with Denmark, issued a
joint statement.

• The statement affirmed that “Greenland belongs to its
people” and that its future can only be decided by Denmark
and Greenland, not external powers.

• In the U.S. Congress, Representative Ruben Gallego (D-
AZ) introduced a resolution to bar federal funds from being
used for any military action or hostilities against
Greenland.
